items.author: Aristotle

items.title: $A^2E$ : An End-to-End Agent Auditing Engine
items.abstract: $A^2E$ is an end-to-end engine for evaluating LLM agents deployed via harnesses. It uses the Agent Task Protocol (ATP) for easy integration and an instrumented Monitor to generate standardized execution traces. This allows for systematic, multidimensional capability assessment beyond simple correctness, offering a more comprehensive evaluation of agent performance.

items.title: Adapting Technical-Service LLM Agents with Latent Logic Augmentation, Robust Noise Reduction, and Hybrid Reward Modeling
items.abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for adapting technical-service LLM agents to production environments. It addresses challenges like hidden decision logic and noisy data by augmenting training with latent logic, robustly filtering noise, and employing a hybrid reward model combining reranking and LLM-as-a-Judge. This approach significantly improves performance and adoption rates on real-world technical-service tasks.

items.title: Alignment Whack-a-Mole : Finetuning Activates Verbatim Recall of Copyrighted Books in Large Language Models
items.abstract: This paper demonstrates that finetuning LLMs, even on unrelated data, can bypass safety mechanisms and enable verbatim recall of copyrighted books. By training models to expand plot summaries, the researchers successfully induced models like GPT-4o and Gemini-2.5-Pro to reproduce large portions of copyrighted works, challenging claims that LLMs do not store copies of their training data.
items.figure_caption: Overview of the extraction pipeline. We generate plot summaries from book excerpts (left), finetune the model to expand summaries into verbatim text (center), and evaluate memorization on held-out books at inference (right).

items.title: Alpha-R1: Alpha Screening with LLM Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: Alpha-R1 uses a reinforcement learning-aligned LLM to screen investment factors. Its core method, "semantic gating," dynamically assesses factors' economic rationale against current market conditions, selecting a sparse, context-aware subset. This approach addresses signal decay and regime shifts by prioritizing factors with relevant economic reasoning, moving beyond purely numerical correlations.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1 . Alpha-R1 Framework Overview. The pipeline follows three sequential stages: (a) Preparation: constructing a global historical memory ( M g ​ l ​ o ​ b ​ a ​ l M_{global} ) from raw data and running systematic factor backtesting; (b) Semantic Construction: mapping quantitative metrics into semantic factor profiles ( \( \alpha \)_{\( \text{des} \)} ) and dynamic market state descriptions ( S t S_{t} ); (c) Reasoning & Optimization: performing semantic gating that evaluates \( \alpha \)_{\( \text{des} \)} against S t S_{t} , with the policy refined through GRPO. Framework diagram showing the preparation, semantic construction, and reasoning and optimization stages of \( \framename \).

items.title: AMA: Adaptive Memory via Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.abstract: AMA introduces a novel framework for LLM agent memory that addresses limitations of existing systems. Its core method involves a multi-agent collaboration to manage memory across multiple granularities, dynamically aligning retrieval granularity with task complexity through a hierarchical memory design. This approach aims to reduce logical inconsistencies and improve the relevance of stored information for complex reasoning.
items.figure_caption: Comparison of static paradigms and the AMA framework. (a) Static methods suffer from the dilemma of fixed granularity, leading to either noise or information loss. (b) AMA dynamically determines the memory granularity to use, aligning retrieval precision with reasoning demands.

items.title: Breaking Planner Integrity Boundary: Enviroment State-Text Injection Attack on LLM-Driven Embodied Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces the Environment State-Text Injection (ESTI) attack, a novel method that targets LLM-driven embodied agents by manipulating their understanding of the environment through deceptive text. Unlike previous attacks, ESTI directly injects false information into the agent's state representation, influencing its planning and potentially leading to incorrect physical execution. The core contribution is demonstrating that environment state text itself can be a vulnerable attack surface, bypassing traditional defenses.
items.figure_caption: Expansion of the security boundary in LLM-driven embodied agents.

items.title: Clarify, Abstain or Answer? Strategising in Conversation with Belief-Augmented Generation
items.abstract: This paper introduces Belief-Augmented Generation (BAG), a method that leverages an LLM's internal uncertainty (represented by multiple generated responses) to inform its conversational strategy. BAG allows LLMs to reason over their own plausible outputs to decide whether to clarify, abstain, or answer, thereby improving accuracy in ambiguous question answering. This approach directly controls generation by grounding it in the model's belief state, unlike prior methods.
items.figure_caption: Turn 1 : User asks a potentially ambiguous question. Turn 2 : BAG samples K K responses, analyses them, and formulates a strategy and response. Turn 3 : BAG asked a clarification question so we simulate a user answer. Turn 4 : Final answer, optionally with another round of BAG. Real Qwen3-14B example.

items.title: Compressing Sequences in the Latent Embedding Space: $K$-Token Merging for Large Language Models
items.abstract: This paper introduces K-Token Merging, a novel method for compressing long prompts in Large Language Models by operating in the latent embedding space. It merges contiguous blocks of token embeddings into single representations using a lightweight encoder, significantly reducing computational and memory costs. This approach achieves substantial input length reduction with minimal performance degradation, positioning itself as a Pareto-optimal solution for efficient LLM processing.

items.title: DSAEval: Evaluating Data Science Agents on a Wide Range of Real-World Data Science Problems
items.abstract: DSAEval introduces a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating data science agents on real-world problems. Its core method involves a multimodal environment with multi-query interactions, allowing agents to tackle diverse data science tasks iteratively. The contribution lies in providing a holistic evaluation framework that assesses agents across reasoning, code, and results, addressing the limitations of existing benchmarks for open-ended data science challenges.
items.figure_caption: Overall performance of all selected models on DSAEval.

items.title: FinAcumen: Financial Multimodal Reasoning via Self-Evolving Experience Memory Harness
items.abstract: FinAcumen addresses the limitations of stateless financial reasoning agents by introducing a novel self-evolving experience memory. This memory bank stores and selectively retrieves successful reasoning strategies and failure patterns from past financial tasks. By conditioning reasoning on relevant past experiences and suppressing irrelevant ones, FinAcumen improves tool routing, retrieval accuracy, and reduces hallucinations, leading to more reliable financial multimodal reasoning.

items.title: Harnessing the Reasoning Economy: A Survey of Efficient Reasoning for Large Language Models
items.abstract: This survey explores "reasoning economy" in Large Language Models (LLMs), aiming to balance task accuracy with computational costs. It analyzes the causes of inefficient reasoning, examines different reasoning patterns, and proposes solutions for both post-training and inference stages to achieve more efficient and effective LLM reasoning.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1. The Landscape of Reasoning Economy

items.title: Inferring the Unspoken: Aligning Embodied Agents with Implicit Preferences
items.abstract: This paper introduces a method called Inferring the Unspoken (InTU) to enable embodied agents to learn implicit user preferences from observed behavior. The core method involves a two-stage process: first, it verbalizes inferred preferences from multimodal demonstrations, and then it uses these verbalized preferences to guide action planning. The main contribution is a new benchmark, Preference-based Planning (PbP), designed for systematically evaluating how well agents can infer and apply these latent preferences in novel situations.

items.title: MCPO: Modality-Contrastive Preference Optimization for Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Compression
items.abstract: This paper introduces Modality-Contrastive Preference Optimization (MCPO) to compress multimodal Chain-of-Thought (M-CoT) reasoning. MCPO uses a novel step-level Normalized Cross-Modal Mutual Information (NCMI) algorithm to identify and prune visually irrelevant reasoning steps. This approach efficiently reduces computational costs and KV-cache pressure in multimodal models without sacrificing reasoning quality.

items.title: Moral Hazard in Multi-Agent Language Models
items.abstract: This paper introduces the Dialogue Moral Hazard Game, a textual environment to study how language agents handle costly, hidden information crucial for team success. The core method involves agents deciding whether to incur a cost to reveal a safety fact benefiting another agent. The key contribution is demonstrating that frontier models like GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Opus 4.8, and Nemotron-3 Ultra exhibit economically rational behavior in this moral hazard setting, closely following theoretical predictions, while other models show varied responses.
items.figure_caption: One successful episode. An agent either preserves local reward or pays to reveal another case’s hidden hazard, posts an anonymous warning, and enables the downstream safe choice.

items.title: OdysSim: Building Foundation Models for Human Behavior Simulation
items.abstract: OdysSim addresses the Sim2Real gap in human behavior simulation by large language models, which tend to become overly agreeable. The paper introduces SOUL, a taxonomy unifying 62 datasets and 23 tasks, and the OdysSim corpus. Their contribution is an end-to-end training method and an open 8B model that achieves state-of-the-art performance on many simulation tasks.
items.figure_caption: Benchmark results on human simulation tasks.

items.title: Provable Pluralistic Alignment: Multi-Party RLHF under Offline Human Feedback
items.abstract: This paper addresses pluralistic alignment in RLHF, where conflicting stakeholder preferences must be reconciled into a single policy. The core method involves jointly estimating party-specific rewards and optimizing a policy pessimistically under various social welfare objectives (Nash, Utilitarian, Egalitarian). The key contribution is providing provable, finite-sample guarantees for both reward estimation and policy suboptimality, even with general, non-scalar, and cyclic preferences.

items.title: Teaching agentic AI to generalize expert diagnostic reasoning in rare diseases
items.abstract: This paper introduces liteOdyssey, an agentic AI trained to generalize expert diagnostic reasoning for rare diseases. Its core method, Policy Iteration with Human Feedback, iteratively refines a natural-language policy based on expert corrections, enabling the AI to execute reusable diagnostic strategies. The key contribution is demonstrating significant improvements in rare disease diagnosis accuracy and policy transferability across different models and datasets, even for unseen diseases.

items.title: The Geometry of Refusal: Why Post-Hoc Safety Is Fragile and Pretraining-Time Safety Persists
items.abstract: This paper argues that post-hoc safety training methods like RLHF are fragile because they only "mask" undesirable behaviors rather than truly removing them. The core method analyzes the geometric relationship between safety updates and the model's existing capabilities, showing that safety updates are often orthogonal to capability directions. The main contribution is demonstrating that this geometric "suppression regime" explains why safety can be easily undone by subsequent fine-tuning, unlike safety learned during pretraining.

items.title: The Little Book of Generative AI Foundations: An Intuitive Mathematical Primer
items.abstract: This book offers an intuitive, derivation-focused mathematical primer on generative AI. It connects key generative model families, including VAEs, diffusion models, GANs, and normalizing flows, by building a coherent understanding of their underlying mathematical principles. The core contribution is making the structure and derivation of these models accessible to a broad audience without sacrificing mathematical rigor.

items.title: To Mix or To Merge: Toward Multi-Domain Reinforcement Learning for Large Language Models
items.abstract: This paper investigates how to train Large Language Models (LLMs) for multi-domain reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). It compares two training approaches: mixing tasks during training versus training separately and then merging models. The core contribution is a comprehensive experimental analysis showing that RLVR across different domains exhibits minimal interference, suggesting that a mixed training approach can effectively achieve expert-level performance across multiple reasoning-intensive tasks.
items.figure_caption: The two training paradigms for multi-domain RLVR: mixed multi-task training and separate training followed by model merging.

items.title: Fable 5.1 Solves the Cyphral Distich, a 370-year-old cipher
items.summary: Fable 5.1, an AI model, has successfully deciphered the Cyphral Distich, a complex 370-year-old cipher, marking a significant breakthrough in cryptanalysis.

items.title: Garry Tan wants US open-weight AI labs to 'distill' frontier models, too
items.summary: Y Combinator's Garry Tan advocates for US open-weight AI labs to distill powerful frontier models, promoting accessibility and competition.

items.title: Open-source AI and open models reading list
items.summary: This reading list compiles essential resources for understanding and engaging with the rapidly evolving landscape of open-source AI and open models.

items.description: Run frontier MoE models on hardware you already own — pure C, zero deps, experts streamed from disk. Tiny engine, immense model. 🐦
items.summary: Colibri is a C-based inference engine that enables running large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models on personal hardware by streaming experts from disk, offering a tiny engine for immense models with zero dependencies.

items.summary: Ever Gauzy is an open-source business management platform offering integrated ERP, CRM, HRM, ATS, and PM functionalities to streamline operations.

items.summary: This repository provides a real-time, open-source spatial intelligence platform that functions as a spy satellite simulator in your browser, displaying live data on a photorealistic 3D globe.

items.description: The secure, validated skill registry for professional AI coding agents. Extend Antigravity, Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot and more with absolute confidence.
items.summary: This repository provides a secure, validated registry of AI coding agent skills, enabling users to confidently extend tools like Antigravity, Claude Code, Cursor, and Copilot.

items.description: Open-source AI sales OS — self-hosted CRM with native AI agents + WhatsApp (WAHA). Open alternative to Kommo, Octadesk & Intercom for any business that sells by chat. MCP-ready, multi-tenant, LGPD.
items.summary: DeskcommCRM is an open-source, self-hosted AI sales OS that functions as a CRM with native AI agents and WhatsApp integration, offering an open alternative to platforms like Kommo for chat-based sales businesses.

items.description: World's first open-source, agentic video production system. 12 production pipelines, 100+ tools, 700+ agent skill and production-knowledge files. Turn your AI coding assistant into a full video production studio.
items.summary: OpenMontage is the first open-source, agentic video production system, offering 12 pipelines and over 100 tools to transform AI coding assistants into comprehensive video studios.

items.description: Extracted system prompts from Anthropic - Claude Fable 5.1, Opus 5, Claude Design, Claude Code. OpenAI - ChatGPT GPT-6-Astra, Codex. Google - Gemini 3.8 Flash, 3.1 Pro, Antigravity. xAI - Grok, Grok Bot, Cursor, Kimi and more! Updated regularly.
items.summary: This repository extracts and compiles system prompts from various AI models like Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Grok, offering a regularly updated collection for researchers and developers.

items.description: Fully autonomous AI Agents system capable of performing complex penetration testing tasks
items.summary: Pentagi is a fully autonomous AI agent system designed to execute complex penetration testing tasks independently.

items.description: YuE2: frontier music generation with symbolic planning, zero-shot covers, and agentic music editing.
items.summary: YuE2 is a frontier music generation system that uses symbolic planning for zero-shot covers and agentic editing to create and manipulate music.

The contribution lies in providing a holistic evaluation framework that assesses agents across reasoning, code, and results, addressing the limitations of existing benchmarks for open-ended data science challenges.
papers.figure_caption: Overall performance of all selected models on DSAEval.

papers.title: FinAcumen: Financial Multimodal Reasoning via Self-Evolving Experience Memory Harness
papers.abstract: FinAcumen addresses the limitations of stateless financial reasoning agents by introducing a novel self-evolving experience memory. This memory bank stores and selectively retrieves successful reasoning strategies and failure patterns from past financial tasks. By conditioning reasoning on relevant past experiences and suppressing irrelevant ones, FinAcumen improves tool routing, retrieval accuracy, and reduces hallucinations, leading to more reliable financial multimodal reasoning.

papers.title: Harnessing the Reasoning Economy: A Survey of Efficient Reasoning for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: This survey explores "reasoning economy" in Large Language Models (LLMs), aiming to balance task accuracy with computational costs. It analyzes the causes of inefficient reasoning, examines different reasoning patterns, and proposes solutions for both post-training and inference stages to achieve more efficient and effective LLM reasoning.
papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. The Landscape of Reasoning Economy

papers.title: Inferring the Unspoken: Aligning Embodied Agents with Implicit Preferences
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a method called Inferring the Unspoken (InTU) to enable embodied agents to learn implicit user preferences from observed behavior. The core method involves a two-stage process: first, it verbalizes inferred preferences from multimodal demonstrations, and then it uses these verbalized preferences to guide action planning. The main contribution is a new benchmark, Preference-based Planning (PbP), designed for systematically evaluating how well agents can infer and apply these latent preferences in novel situations.

papers.title: MCPO: Modality-Contrastive Preference Optimization for Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Compression
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Modality-Contrastive Preference Optimization (MCPO) to compress multimodal Chain-of-Thought (M-CoT) reasoning. MCPO uses a novel step-level Normalized Cross-Modal Mutual Information (NCMI) algorithm to identify and prune visually irrelevant reasoning steps. This approach efficiently reduces computational costs and KV-cache pressure in multimodal models without sacrificing reasoning quality.

papers.title: Moral Hazard in Multi-Agent Language Models
papers.abstract: This paper introduces the Dialogue Moral Hazard Game, a textual environment to study how language agents handle costly, hidden information crucial for team success. The core method involves agents deciding whether to incur a cost to reveal a safety fact benefiting another agent. The key contribution is demonstrating that frontier models like GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Opus 4.8, and Nemotron-3 Ultra exhibit economically rational behavior in this moral hazard setting, closely following theoretical predictions, while other models show varied responses.
papers.figure_caption: One successful episode. An agent either preserves local reward or pays to reveal another case’s hidden hazard, posts an anonymous warning, and enables the downstream safe choice.

papers.title: OdysSim: Building Foundation Models for Human Behavior Simulation
papers.abstract: OdysSim addresses the Sim2Real gap in human behavior simulation by large language models, which tend to become overly agreeable. The paper introduces SOUL, a taxonomy unifying 62 datasets and 23 tasks, and the OdysSim corpus. Their contribution is an end-to-end training method and an open 8B model that achieves state-of-the-art performance on many simulation tasks.
papers.figure_caption: Benchmark results on human simulation tasks.

papers.title: Provable Pluralistic Alignment: Multi-Party RLHF under Offline Human Feedback
papers.abstract: This paper addresses pluralistic alignment in RLHF, where conflicting stakeholder preferences must be reconciled into a single policy. The core method involves jointly estimating party-specific rewards and optimizing a policy pessimistically under various social welfare objectives (Nash, Utilitarian, Egalitarian). The key contribution is providing provable, finite-sample guarantees for both reward estimation and policy suboptimality, even with general, non-scalar, and cyclic preferences.

papers.title: Teaching agentic AI to generalize expert diagnostic reasoning in rare diseases
papers.abstract: This paper introduces liteOdyssey, an agentic AI trained to generalize expert diagnostic reasoning for rare diseases. Its core method, Policy Iteration with Human Feedback, iteratively refines a natural-language policy based on expert corrections, enabling the AI to execute reusable diagnostic strategies. The key contribution is demonstrating significant improvements in rare disease diagnosis accuracy and policy transferability across different models and datasets, even for unseen diseases.

papers.title: The Geometry of Refusal: Why Post-Hoc Safety Is Fragile and Pretraining-Time Safety Persists
papers.abstract: This paper argues that post-hoc safety training methods like RLHF are fragile because they only "mask" undesirable behaviors rather than truly removing them. The core method analyzes the geometric relationship between safety updates and the model's existing capabilities, showing that safety updates are often orthogonal to capability directions. The main contribution is demonstrating that this geometric "suppression regime" explains why safety can be easily undone by subsequent fine-tuning, unlike safety learned during pretraining.

papers.title: The Little Book of Generative AI Foundations: An Intuitive Mathematical Primer
papers.abstract: This book offers an intuitive, derivation-focused mathematical primer on generative AI. It connects key generative model families, including VAEs, diffusion models, GANs, and normalizing flows, by building a coherent understanding of their underlying mathematical principles. The core contribution is making the structure and derivation of these models accessible to a broad audience without sacrificing mathematical rigor.

papers.title: To Mix or To Merge: Toward Multi-Domain Reinforcement Learning for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: This paper investigates how to train Large Language Models (LLMs) for multi-domain reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). It compares two training approaches: mixing tasks during training versus training separately and then merging models. The core contribution is a comprehensive experimental analysis showing that RLVR across different domains exhibits minimal interference, suggesting that a mixed training approach can effectively achieve expert-level performance across multiple reasoning-intensive tasks.
papers.figure_caption: The two training paradigms for multi-domain RLVR: mixed multi-task training and separate training followed by model merging.
